subtitle: Design With the People Who Live the System
title: Policy becomes real through people's experience
paragraph: We combine what the data measures with what people experience.

orbitItems.label: Listen
orbitItems.description: Understand needs, behaviours, frustrations, incentives and barriers.

orbitItems.label: Map
orbitItems.description: Visualise journeys, service interactions, processes and failure points.

orbitItems.label: Co-Design
orbitItems.description: Develop ideas with users, client teams and technical stakeholders.

orbitItems.label: Prototype
orbitItems.description: Build the smallest useful representation of the policy, service or model.

orbitItems.label: Iterate
orbitItems.description: Keep what works. Change what does not.

iterateText: Keep what works. Change what does not.
questionText: Why technically correct reforms still fail
questionAnswer: Even the most well-designed policies fail when they don't account for the lived experience of the people who must implement and use them. Technical correctness alone is insufficient without human-centered design.
